result.title: WASP: Continual Weight Adaptation for Streaming LLM Personalization
result.summary: Personalized large language models (LLMs) should continually adapt to users' evolving preferences. Yet extracting preference changes from noisy interaction histories while supporting inexpensive updates remains challenging. We introduce WASP (Weight Adaptation for Streaming Personalization), a recurrent framework that captures fine-grained preferences directly from raw user interactions and generates personalized LoRA adapters without expensive per-user optimization. Specifically, WASP achieves this by training a shared hypernetwork that maintains a compact user representation and outputs adapter weights in a single forward pass. As new interactions arrive, WASP updates this representation without reprocessing full interaction history, enabling continual adaptation with per-update costs independent of history length. Experiments on personalization benchmarks and chronological interaction streams show that WASP sustains high-quality personalization over long horizons under fixed compute and storage budgets. Together, these results support efficient streaming personalization and facilitate privacy-preserving on-device deployment.

AI.brief_summary: WASP 面向流式 LLM 个性化，训练一个共享超网络，从原始交互中维护紧凑用户表示并单次前向生成个性化 LoRA 适配器，新交互到来时增量更新该表示而无需重跑全部历史。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「循环紧凑状态＋超网络生成权重、单次更新成本与历史长度无关」的机制可供核查是否能映射到 LVR 中固定预算的 latent 工作区更新与长度泛化，但该文针对纯文本个性化，与视觉证据和推理状态的关系需人工判断。
